design: 48 nonlinear additive worlds with nonlinear-aware local Bayesian inference using raw-parent plus tanh(parent) features; width1 vs uniform width2
interpretation: Partial world-model repair significantly improves absolute edge recovery for both width1 and width2 on the identical nonlinear worlds. Once the model is less wrong, width2 again shows higher true-DAG posterior mass with a resolved paired gain, higher MAP recovery, and lower mean edge error, although the edge-error CI still crosses zero. Proposal breadth and world-model adequacy therefore interact rather than contributing independently.
